scenarios.title: Living alone, year-round
scenarios.summary: A permanent resident who wants a compact home, a short walk to the lodge and a clear maintenance routine.
scenarios.space: ~27 m² clear plus porch; one sleeping room, living/kitchen and bathroom.
scenarios.storage: A small exterior locker, porch storage and a loft/bed storage plan. No basement.
scenarios.winter: Cold-climate heat pump, vestibule, drain-down and a snow-clearing routine.
scenarios.access: Step-free porch route, but the current bathroom does not fit a 1.5 m turning circle.
scenarios.privacy: A separate clearing and screened porch; the lodge is a short walk away.
scenarios.work: A desk in the living room; connectivity needs a real service test, not a map promise.
scenarios.shared: Lodge laundry, workshop, guest room and community meals.
scenarios.responsibilities: Path clearing, shared-system checks, a buddy check-in and a role in the fire plan.
scenarios.unresolved: Overnight care, illness, isolation and how a solo resident gets help quickly.

scenarios.title: A couple working remotely
scenarios.summary: Two people who need reliable work space, power and bandwidth without turning the home into an office.
scenarios.space: ~50 m² clear; separate work corner or second-module studio; two screens and a call space.
scenarios.storage: Files, equipment and bikes need dedicated storage; the porch is not a warehouse.
scenarios.winter: Heat pump, balanced ventilation and a power/backup plan for workdays.
scenarios.access: Step-free route; verify door widths, thresholds and a place for mobility equipment.
scenarios.privacy: Two people need acoustic separation; the pair plan has to be tested, not assumed.
scenarios.work: A service test for fibre/fixed wireless; shared lodge meeting room as overflow.
scenarios.shared: Lodge meeting room, guest room, workshop and laundry.
scenarios.responsibilities: Shared internet contract, backup power, snow clearing and quiet-hours norms.
scenarios.unresolved: Bandwidth, latency, backup power and whether remote work is compatible with a seasonal community.

scenarios.title: A seasonal resident
scenarios.summary: A summer and shoulder-season resident who does not need a year-round home and should not pretend a 20-ft cabin is one.
scenarios.space: ~12.8 m² clear; one compact bedroom, bathroom and living/kitchen.
scenarios.storage: Very limited; a separate locker and the lodge store are essential.
scenarios.winter: The compact cabin is not presented as a year-round accessible home; water, heat and road access need a winter strategy.
scenarios.access: Compact bathroom and tight circulation; not suitable for a wheelchair user without redesign.
scenarios.privacy: A low, juniper-edged site with a separate porch view.
scenarios.work: Occasional desk use only; do not assume a permanent office.
scenarios.shared: Lodge laundry, guest space, tools and the main gathering space.
scenarios.responsibilities: Seasonal opening/closing, water drain-down, wildlife-proofing and shared fees.
scenarios.unresolved: Whether winter occupation is permitted, insurable and safe; short-term rental rules.

scenarios.title: Planning for changing mobility
scenarios.summary: An older resident who wants to stay in the community as mobility changes, without assuming the current compact plan is accessible.
scenarios.space: A longer room or a different plan is needed for a 1.5 m turning circle; the current bathroom fails.
scenarios.storage: Reachable storage, no ladder-only storage, space for mobility equipment.
scenarios.winter: Reliable heat, backup power, a clear accessible path and a place to wait for help.
scenarios.access: Step-free entry is only the start; bathroom, sleeping and kitchen clearances need redesign.
scenarios.privacy: A quiet site, but the resident needs to be reachable in an emergency.
scenarios.work: Optional; a seated work surface and good light.
scenarios.shared: Lodge universal washroom, meals and guest space; not a substitute for personal care.
scenarios.responsibilities: Accessible path maintenance, emergency check-in and a personal support plan.
scenarios.unresolved: Personal care, funding, home modifications, evacuation and aging in place without a care facility.

scenarios.title: A household that hosts guests
scenarios.summary: A resident who wants occasional family and friends to stay without letting visitors take over the hamlet.
scenarios.space: A second sleeping room or a convertible studio; a guest bathroom is better than a shared one.
scenarios.storage: Guest bedding, chairs, parking and outdoor gear need a home.
scenarios.winter: Extra heat and water demand; a guest wing should be closable.
scenarios.access: Guest route and bathroom should be step-free; visitors may have different needs.
scenarios.privacy: Visitor rules, quiet hours and a clear boundary around the resident's rooms.
scenarios.work: Noise and call conflicts; guests need a place to work if they stay.
scenarios.shared: Lodge guest room, parking, laundry and gathering space.
scenarios.responsibilities: Booking rules, cleaning, insurance, water use and neighbourhood courtesy.
scenarios.unresolved: Short-term rental versus private hosting; parking, septic load and insurance.

scenarios.title: Gardening and land stewardship
scenarios.summary: A resident who wants to grow food, compost and care for the forest, with realistic water and wildlife constraints.
scenarios.space: A home plus a small mudroom/utility zone for tools and produce.
scenarios.storage: Tool storage, harvest storage, potting bench and a place to dry boots.
scenarios.winter: Seed starting, freeze protection and a water plan that does not empty the fire reserve.
scenarios.access: Raised beds and a firm route; gardening still needs a seated option.
scenarios.privacy: Garden is shared or semi-private; clear rules prevent quiet encroachment.
scenarios.work: A seasonal work pattern; not assumed to be a paid farm.
scenarios.shared: Community garden, compost, tool library, lodge kitchen and water.
scenarios.responsibilities: Watering rota, compost management, invasive-species control and deer/fire clearance.
scenarios.unresolved: Soil contamination, water rights, food safety, wildlife and who owns the harvest.

initial: Land acquisition
Purchase or long-term lease, legal fees, title, survey and closing costs.
Surveys and professional studies
Survey, geotechnical, environmental, archaeology, species at risk, fire and accessibility studies.
Planning and approvals
Planning application, zoning, consent, conservation authority and building permits.
Roads and access
Entrance, lane, turnaround, bridge/culvert, snow storage and emergency access.
Water and wastewater
Wells/cisterns, treatment, septic/alternative systems, testing and connections.
Shared electrical infrastructure
Service, distribution, backup power, metering and utility coordination.
Common lodge
Structure, envelope, kitchen, laundry, universal washroom and shared systems.
Container acquisition
Units, inspection, survey, repair and delivery coordination.
Fabrication
Cuts, reinforcement, frames, insulation, cladding, windows and services.
Transport and installation
Crane, permits, route survey, rigging, temporary works and site supervision.
Foundations
Piles, footings, geotechnical work, drainage and frost protection.
Contingency
Unknown conditions, design changes, weather and approval delays.
recurring: Land taxes
Municipal property taxes and any school/regional levies.
Insurance
Property, liability, wildfire, flood and shared-asset coverage.
Snow clearing
Lane, parking, paths and emergency access.
Road maintenance
Grading, gravel, culverts, bridge inspection and drainage.
Shared utilities
Common electricity, water treatment, septic servicing and communications.
Wastewater maintenance
Pumping, inspection, repairs and reserve-field planning.
Building maintenance
Roof, envelope, porches, paint, seals and structural inspection.
Ecological stewardship
Invasive species, trail work, tree risk, fire-fuel maintenance and monitoring.
Governance and administration
Bookkeeping, insurance, meetings, legal and record keeping.
Capital replacement reserves
Roof, pump, cistern, road and shared-building replacements.
individual: The resident's own dwelling cost, financing and professional fees.
Ground lease/occupancy payment, if any, set by the land trust.
Home electricity, heating, water/sewer share and internet.
Repairs and replacements inside the resident's responsibility.
Contents and dwelling coverage as applicable.
Residents' association fees for shared services and reserves.
costs.note: Categories only. No land, construction, insurance or utility prices are invented. Every number must be entered from a real quote, local data or a clearly labelled assumption.

Who decides, who owns, who can leave?

roadmap.title: Investigate jurisdictions and sites
questions: Which municipality/First Nation territory?

roadmap.title: Preliminary planning and zoning
questions: Are six homes, a lodge and shared water permitted?

roadmap.title: Environmental constraints
questions: Wetland, shoreline, species at risk, archaeology, slope, flooding?
Can the footprint avoid harm?

roadmap.title: Water, wastewater and emergency access
questions: Is there safe potable water?
Can sewage be treated?
Can fire/ambulance reach every home?

roadmap.title: Financing and insurance
questions: Who funds shared infrastructure?

roadmap.title: Architectural and engineering studies
questions: Do the homes meet structure, fire, energy and accessibility requirements?
What needs redesign?

What conditions apply?

questions: Who builds, inspects and maintains it?

living: Winter roads and paths
Shared lane/parking clearing and a written snow plan.
Residents clear their own porch/path and keep emergency access clear.
Snow storage, ice, plowing costs and who is responsible when someone is away.
Grocery and medical access
Shared trips and delivery coordination.
Personal shopping, prescriptions and appointments.
Distance, winter driving, no car, and privacy of health information.
Internet and mobile
Shared service contract and a lodge connection.
Home router, backup and data use.
No guarantee of fibre; trees, terrain and weather affect service.
Power outages
Shared battery/solar and a lodge refuge.
Home backup, medical equipment and frozen pipes.
A battery is not a permanent generator; fuel and maintenance matter.
Water shortages
Shared storage, fire reserve and trigger levels.
Home demand, leaks and personal use.
A fire reserve cannot be spent on gardens.
Wastewater
Shared septic/alternative system servicing.
What goes down the drain; reporting problems.
Pumping, reserve fields, flooding and replacement cost.
Shared laundry
Lodge machines, booking and maintenance.
Personal laundry and supplies.
Queues, noise, accessibility and machine downtime.
Deliveries
Shared address, parcel box and delivery rules.
Personal orders and access.
Rural carriers, theft, winter access and traffic.
Visitors and guests
Guest room and visitor rules.
Hosting, parking and quiet hours.
Privacy, septic load, insurance and short-term rental rules.
Pets
Shared rules for dogs, waste and wildlife.
Feeding, control, vaccinations and noise.
Wildlife conflict, allergies and liability.
Noise
Quiet hours and shared-space norms.
Home music, tools and guests.
Small homes transmit sound; consensus is not the same as enforcement.
Shared tools
Tool library, maintenance and training.
Borrowing, returning and damage.
Storage, safety and replacement.
Gardening
Community garden, compost and water rules.
Personal beds and harvest.
Soil, deer, water, invasives and who owns the food.
Wildlife
Bear-safe storage, no feeding and reporting.
Home screening, pets and waste.
Living with wildlife is not a pest-control problem alone.
Emergency response
Address signs, fire water, access and phone tree.
Personal medication, mobility and meet-up plan.
Response times, evacuation and care during a long outage.
Privacy and conflict
Clear shared/private boundaries and a dispute process.
Home privacy, visitors and personal information.
Small communities can blur boundaries; governance must protect dissent.
Accessibility
Step-free shared facilities, hearing loop and accessible meetings.
Home modifications, mobility equipment and personal support.
A step-free door does not make a compact bathroom or a winter path accessible.
